overclaims: '27% of sessions contain a user doesn't want to proceed rejection ... a direct measure of a human answering a permission prompt.' The 34/126 counts every cc_interrupt_reject result. 1 of the 59 is '[Request interrupted' (only 33 sessions have the quoted text), and 18/59 are on ExitPlanMode/AskUserQuestion, which are plan approvals and questions, not permission prompts. Counting only permission-gated tools: 41 results in 20/126 sessions = 15.9% [10.5, 23.2]. The minimum latency is 0.164 s.

'The same marker means machine denial in cc_local and human interaction in swechat.' This is wrong; the two corpora use different markers for these. cc_permission_denied is machine-fast in both: swechat n 3, p50 0.022 s, max 0.037; cc_local n 173, p50 0.007 s. cc_interrupt_reject is human-paced in both: swechat p50 23.4 s; cc_local 9 results, p50 4.9 s. What differs between the corpora is frequency, not meaning.

Notes Part 2 says human-wait evidence is 'absent in aiv_cc and cc_local'. For cc_local the probe's own JSON shows 9 cc_interrupt_reject results in 6/107 sessions (5.6% [2.6, 11.7]), p50 4.9 s, 6 of them shell. Only 'no waits on Edit/Write' (0/358) is supported.

aiv_cc: 'a call that is not the last tool_use block of its message absorbs the generation time of the later blocks ... tool execution streams in the CLI but not in this SDK version.' 160 of the 165 not-last file_write calls come from 1 session. For other tools, not-last results usually arrive before the last block's stamp: grep 41/41, read 45/68, get_events 502/993, chat_message 187/294, shell 549/1,570. Not-last Read is faster than last (p50 0.111 vs 0.314 s). Execution evidently does stream in the SDK for most tools; this is a one-session Write effect.

aiv_cc: 'That is the ingestion floor' and 'insert time tracks event time'. The minimum inter-row gap is 18.2 ms, so inserts alone can be that close, while call-to-result is never under 46 ms. The ~50 ms is a pipeline floor of unidentified cause. The match with event time is shown only at run level: 82 run spans vs SDK duration_ms, p50 -3.7 ms, p5 -0.244 s, p95 0.128 s. Per-event insert lag is unmeasured. The 'additive offset' also varies (Glob excess p5 0.019 to p50 0.049 s, 1/90 negative), so it is not a constant.

'15% of long shell commands start more than 2 s after the call (bash_progress offset).' The 373 calls include 6 Task (subagent) calls linked through parent_call_id. All 6 are over 2 s (p50 68.9 s), and that is subagent run time, not a pre-exec wait. Shell only: 50/367 = 13.6% [5.8, 25.9], before the ~1 s rounding from the integer elapsedTimeSeconds.

'Human waits are clearly present: 13.2% [6.8, 21.7] of Edit/Write calls take more than 2 s.' The probe's own recorded reason for the 2 s threshold says it captures human prompts, hooks or slow file systems, so this is not a direct human measure. Hooks do not explain it (182/296 slow edits have no hook event). It is concentrated: 187/296 slow edits sit in 5 sessions, 51/115 sessions have any, and 230/296 are in sessions that also have a rejection. It shows waits in a minority of sessions, not a corpus-wide property.

'The heavy right tails are real waits: the maximum is 78,675.7 s, a subagent.' The maximum is a main-thread Task call (is_subagent False) lasting about 21.9 h, and that subagent's own inner calls also show ~78,443 s deltas. This fits a suspended or resumed session. 'Real waits' is asserted, not measured.
'The last native digit is uniform' is backed by a swechat-pooled chi2 p of 0.20. OpenCode alone, on 8,298 distinct stamps, gives p 0.039. Minor, and it does not affect any verdict.

overclaims: Notes section 7 says conservation 'can carry a mechanism only where the fit is tight' and then lists Gemini CLI and SWE-chat Claude Code, with the result-only form or with thinking chars. Under the pre-registered rule neither is TIGHT. Gemini CLI result-only has a Spearman CI low of 0.857, below 0.90. SWE-chat CC with thinking gives 90.1/168.7 = 0.53, which is LOOSE. And SWE-chat CC has no exact output counts, so the result-only form does not apply to it.
Caveats say 'every residual is an upper bound on what a real tokenizer would give'. This is unproven: the chars-to-tokens error is not guaranteed to only inflate residuals.

aiv_cc TIGHT is reported with session-clustered CIs (Spearman [0.977, 0.988], residual [53.1, 82.9], ratio [0.038, 0.054]). All 27491 fit pairs come from one sdk_session_id (one agent, one resumed conversation, 73 runs). The CIs treat dependent runs as independent, so TIGHT holds for one agent and harness, not for the corpus type in general.

'A tool result whose logged length differs ... by more than about a quarter of a typical result sits outside the p90 of honest pairs' is a claim about detection power. No manipulated results were injected to test it, and the p90 comes from that single agent.

The single-split cross-fit residuals are reported with CIs that keep the fit fixed, which hides fold variance in small groups. For Gemini CLI (11 sessions), 117.8 is below the 5th percentile of 50 random session splits (median 148.1). For Codex (15 sessions), 315.3 is above the 95th percentile (median 258.9).

Codex is framed as 'No, as measured', with residual 2.3x and result-only 2.783x a typical result. Subtracting the full usage_out, reasoning included, gives a residual of 45 tokens (about 0.33 of a typical result, Spearman 0.974). The failure comes from the pre-registered visible-output-only choice, not from conservation itself.
aiv_cu Anthropic's 'decisive' pooled Spearman of 0.323 is a pooling artifact: every stratum on its own is 0.41-0.70. The verdict is unaffected, but the number understates per-stratum conservation.

'Screenshot tool results are counted exactly and apart from text' (Gemini IMAGE modality) overstates slightly. It is a total over all images in the prompt, identified with screenshots only by inference. 3 of 420 GUI gaps show no rise, and it cannot split several images in one gap.

The TIGHT vs LOOSE contrast between aiv_cc and SWE-chat CC comes mostly from the denominator: absolute residuals are 66 vs 125 tokens (1.9x), but typical results are 1447.7 vs 168.7 tokens (8.6x). aiv_cc's 'Yes' partly reflects its very large tool results. prereg.verdict_rules:
All rules are fixed in prereg.json and implemented mechanically. Every number below is in prereg.json resolved, prereg_calibration.json or phase_a.json.

Global rules:
- Session-clustered CIs via lib/stats (1,000 draws, seed 20261003).
- Rates need a denominator of at least 30 from at least 5 sessions; below that a cell is INSUFFICIENT_N.
- Zero-count rates use the per-event Wilson upper bound.
- aiv_cc verdicts are always labelled single-agent case study.

Probe 1 (latency physics):
- No-human-wait filter: the A1 proposal, pre-registered. It keeps 2,387 of 13,589 swechat CC pairs on A.
- FLAT kill: a tool is FLAT if its delta IQR is at most 2x the stamp resolution, or its IQR of log10 delta is below 0.05. The unit is DEAD if every work-bound tool is FLAT. On A the smallest work-bound IQR is 0.101.
- Generation-time model: T_gen = chars x 0.25 / G90, and r = latency / T_gen. G90 is the A-split p90 output rate: swechat CC 65.3, cc_local 91.4, aiv_cc 47.1 (char-based), codex 76.5, opencode 62.5, gemini 94.3 tokens/s. Only pairs with T_gen of at least 1 s count.
- fp_share (share of work-bound pairs with r >= 1): ALIVE if <= 0.05 with CI hi <= 0.10; WEAK if <= 0.20; else DEAD.
- AUC (generation-bound vs work-bound): ALIVE if >= 0.85 with CI lo >= 0.75; WEAK if >= 0.70; else DEAD.
- Unit verdict: ALIVE needs both ALIVE. Without a generation-bound control the unit is at most WEAK.
- Downgrade: ALIVE becomes WEAK if the floor is UNSTABLE (more than 10% of series have a factor-2 step at p <= 0.01, minimum segment 20) or if most tools shift relative to their A p5 floors.

Probe 2 (knowledge precedence):
- Primary statistic S_deep: the share of successful first-try deep accesses that are unsourced and not enumerated.
- Deep thresholds D per unit from A p75: swechat CC 6, opencode 6, gemini 3, cc_local 3, aiv_cc 6, others the pooled 6.
- ALIVE if S_deep <= 0.05 with CI hi <= 0.10; WEAK if <= 0.20; DEAD if > 0.20. Minimum 100 accesses from 20 sessions; otherwise the rule falls back to S_path_any, capped at WEAK.
- Instrument check: swechat CC edit old_string symbols must be unsourced at <= 0.10, or every Probe 2 verdict is capped at WEAK.

Probe 3 (pushback):
- Long session = paired calls >= the A p75 (L75): swechat CC 134, cc_local 20, aiv_cc 666, codex 120, opencode 185, gemini 405, aiv_cu 40, whowhen AG 3. L90 is secondary.
- Zero-error tail Z (share of long sessions with no errors): ALIVE if Z <= 0.10 with Wilson hi <= 0.20 and n_long >= 30; WEAK if <= 0.30; else DEAD; fewer than 20 long sessions is INSUFFICIENT_N.
- Reaction: the retry effect R_fail - R_ok, where a retry is the same tool with Jaccard >= 0.5. ALIVE if CI lo >= 0.10; WEAK if CI lo > 0; else DEAD.
- Early vs late: descriptive only.

Probe 4 (entropy):
- Hex tokens of length 7/8/32/40/64 with at least one digit and one letter. The chi-square uses expected counts conditioned on that filter. Effect size: w_adj = sqrt(max(0, (chi2 - 15) / N)).
- N_min = 1,131 symbols (power 0.8 for w = 0.15 at alpha 0.01).
- Instrument: the control (M_git, else M_all) must have w_adj CI hi <= 0.15. On A: swechat CC 0.055, aiv_cc 0.081, opencode 0.107, aiv_cu 0.121.
- ALIVE if the unsourced model-typed class (T_orig) has w_adj >= 0.15 and its CI lo is above the control's CI hi; WEAK if its point is above the control's CI hi; DEAD if its point is at or below it.
- Round numbers are compared against the machine class (M_all), not against 0.1, because machine last-0 shares are already 0.111 to 0.316 on A.
